text.p: Switzerland, spearheaded by Australian Open winner Martina Hingis, beat Slovakia 3-2 in their Fed Cup World group two first round tie on Sunday.

The Kosice-born Hingis, 16, back in her hometown for the first time in 13 years, won both her singles matches against Katarina Studenikova and Karina Habsudova in straight sets and then teamed up with Patty Schnyder to beat Habsudova and Radka Zrubakova 6-0 6-1 in the decisive doubles.
"This was a tremendous effort by the entire team and we put up a great performance," Swiss team captain Melanie Molitorova, Hingis's mother and coach, said afterwards.
With her performance in Kosice, Hingis maintained her unbeaten record this year and said her three wins had further boosted her self-confidence.
"I think I still have plenty of reserves and over the weekend I made no mistakes. This gives me the confidence that I can beat anybody in the world," said a smiling Hingis.
Present during the entire tie was Martina's father, Karol, who works as a groundkeeper in a local tennis club and also as a coach for juniors.
After most of Martina's wins, Karol came down to kiss his daughter in congratulation.
The two have rarely seen each other since Molitorova, who has reassumed her maiden name, and Martina emigrated to Switzerland eight years ago.
"I think my father was keeping his fingers crossed for me even though I was actually playing against his country," Hingis said.

Hingis, currently number two in the world, will become one of the youngest players to head the rankings at the end of March when she will take over from Germany's Steffi Graf. Graf is injured and will be unable to defend her last year's titles in Key Biscayne and Indian Wells.
